title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
lede: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre reports a sharp rise in attacks run with autonomous hacking tools, and says they succeed through old, unmitigated weaknesses rather than new exploits.

points: Since September the NCSC has seen several incidents involving autonomous tools, some causing intrusions and downtime.
The tools resemble the penetration-testing software defenders use; open-source examples such as Artex and Cairn are free to download.
Agents typically hunt for internet-facing systems, then cycle through weak passwords or abuse API endpoints developers use to reach data.
The flaws are neither novel memory bugs nor known unpatched CVEs, but technical debt built up over years.
The FBI has separately warned that attackers are using AI pentest tools at unprecedented speed.

sections.text: Exposed developer APIs and guessable credentials that sat unnoticed for years can now be found in minutes, so the NCSC's advice is that ordinary security controls matter more, not less.
